packs.name: Strix-inspired methodology pack
packs.license_note: Reimplemented locally from high-level ideas only.
packs.summary: Evidence-first methodology for Burp-driven triage with strong baseline control, bounded comparisons, and report-grade capture discipline.

baseline_confirmation: Keep one untouched baseline request and one clearly named comparison request before widening the search.
Prefer one variable change at a time and treat status, headers, length, and visible body deltas as separate evidence points.
evidence_priorities: Prioritize role-separated diffs, object-boundary changes, and proof that a server-side control changed, not only client-visible variation.
Capture the exact request pair, exact response pair, and one short analyst note on why the delta matters.
reporting_focus: Write evidence as a chain: baseline -> changed request -> server-side effect -> business impact candidate.
Do not claim a severity promotion until the evidence shows either boundary failure, durable state change, or sensitive data access.
stop_conditions: Stop widening the test when the current delta is still ambiguous or not yet repeatable.
Do not broaden to more payloads until one high-signal comparison is documented cleanly.

workflow_focus: Anchor the issue to one object boundary first, then compare a second tenant or role-owned object of the same type.
If Burp Scanner already marked a second issue on the same flow, use it only when the same object transition explains both findings.
Treat the reflection context as the first proof target: HTML body, attribute, script, JSON, or template render.
Only upgrade once you know who can trigger and who can observe the rendered payload.
Treat XXE as an entity and parser workflow: parser acceptance first, entity handling second, side effect third.
Treat parser behavior, URL normalization, and callback evidence as three separate questions; answer them one at a time.
Keep outbound-fetch hypotheses tied to pasted Burp or Collaborator evidence only.
